title: The city that dances together. | Folkly
description: Behind New Orleans’ second lines is a remarkable social invention: a community that turns looking after one another into a public celebration.

title: A city finds its voice. | Folkly
description: Fado carries the intimacy of Lisbon’s neighborhoods into a much larger world. Its history reveals how a local form can change and still sound unmistakably like home.

title: A living language of color. | Folkly
description: In Oaxaca’s Zapotec weaving traditions, color carries knowledge of land, family, and material. Keeping that knowledge alive also means finding new things to say with it.

title: The future had a Detroit frequency. | Folkly
description: A radio signal, a circle of friends, and a willingness to hear connections: the cultural conditions behind Detroit techno reach beyond the familiar story of machines.

title: The Thread That Holds: Kente, Identity, and the Fight for Survival in Bonwire | Folkly
description: In Bonwire, Ghana, kente weaving carries proverbs and identity through changing markets, family workshops, and debates about the craft’s future.

title: The Weight of the Square: Castells in Tarragona | Folkly
description: In Tarragona, Catalonia, castells turn human towers into a shared practice of trust, training, and belonging in the public square.

title: The Hands That Remember: Kimjang in a Changing Seoul | Folkly
description: Kimjang brings Seoul households and neighbors together to make winter kimchi, passing food knowledge through a changing city.

title: The Star That Wins the Year | Folkly
description: Matariki and Puanga mark the Māori new year through distinct regional traditions of remembrance, seasonal knowledge, and renewal.

title: The Stirring Pot: How Sumanak Anchors Belonging in Dushanbe | Folkly
description: In Dushanbe, Tajikistan, preparing sumanak for Navruz brings neighbors together around a shared pot and the arrival of spring.

title: The Weight of Blue: Indigo, Labor, and the Living Economy of Tokushima | Folkly
description: In Tokushima, Japan, aizome indigo dyeing connects fermentation, skilled labor, and the livelihoods that sustain a living craft.

title: The Living Soil of Xochimilco | Folkly
description: Xochimilco’s chinampas connect canal agriculture, living soil, and local livelihoods in southern Mexico City.
